title: Getting started with scholid
text: scholid exposes small set user-facing functions operate consistently across identifier types: scholid_types() lists supported identifier types. is_scholid(x, type) checks whether values match identifier type. normalize_scholid(x, type) returns canonical identifier strings. extract_scholid(text, type) extracts identifiers free text. classify_scholid(x) guesses identifier type per element. detect_scholid_type(x) detects identifier types canonical wrapped input values (e.g., URLs labels). generic helpers dispatch internally type-specific implementations is_doi(), normalize_orcid(), extract_isbn().

title: Getting started with scholid
text: per-type formats, validation rules, classification order, see Scholarly Identifiers Defined vignette (vignette("scholid_definitions", package = "scholid")), also linked package site identifiers.

title: Getting started with scholid
text: is_scholid() checks whether value valid identifier specific type. expects canonical (near-canonical) input; wrapped forms URLs normalized first. checksum-based types (ORCID, ISBN, ISSN), is_scholid() normalize_scholid() verify checksum. vectorized preserves missing values.
code: x <- c(     "10.1000/182",     "not a doi",     NA ) scholid::is_scholid(     x    = x,     type = "doi" ) ## [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA

title: Getting started with scholid
text: Normalization removes common wrappers enforces canonical representation. particularly useful identifiers stored URLs prefixed labels. ORCID iDs, normalization removes URL prefixes enforces hyphenated grouping. Normalization designed predictable: - NA input stays NA. - Invalid inputs typically become NA_character_.

title: Getting started with scholid
text: Extraction harvesting identifiers unstructured text. result list one element per input element. element character vector matches (possibly empty). list return type intentional: single text string can contain multiple identifiers.
code: txt <- c(   "See https://doi.org/10.1000/182 and doi:10.5555/12345678.",   "No identifier here.",   NA ) scholid::extract_scholid(     text = txt,     type = "doi" ) ## [[1]] ## [1] "10.1000/182"      "10.5555/12345678" ##  ## [[2]] ## character(0) ##  ## [[3]] ## character(0)

title: Getting started with scholid
text: classify_scholid() returns best-guess identifier type per element mixed identifier columns. Classification based set available is_<type>() checks precedence order defined scholid_types().
code: x <- c(   "10.1000/182",   "0000-0002-1825-0097",   "PMC12345",   "2101.00001v2",   "not an id",   NA ) scholid::classify_scholid(x = x) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" "pmcid" "arxiv" NA      NA

title: Getting started with scholid
text: Many identifiers appear wrapped (URLs, prefixes, trailing punctuation). Classification strict expects canonical strings. common pattern : Extract identifiers text. Normalize extracted values. Classify /validate.
code: txt <- "Read https://doi.org/10.1000/182 (and ORCID 0000-0002-1825-0097)." dois <- scholid::extract_scholid(txt, "doi")[[1]] orcids <- scholid::extract_scholid(txt, "orcid")[[1]]  dois_n <- scholid::normalize_scholid(dois, "doi") orcids_n <- scholid::normalize_scholid(orcids, "orcid")  scholid::classify_scholid(c(dois_n, orcids_n)) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" scholid::is_scholid(dois_n, "doi") ## [1] TRUE scholid::is_scholid(orcids_n, "orcid") ## [1] TRUE

title: Getting started with scholid
text: detect_scholid_type() performs best-effort type detection mixed, messy identifier input. contrast classify_scholid(), detection also recognizes common wrapped forms URLs prefixed labels (e.g., doi:, https://orcid.org/, arXiv:, PMID:). Detection useful working raw data identifiers may yet normalized. example, wrapped identifiers classified strictly: However, can detected directly: Whitespace minor formatting irregularities handled conservatively: detect_scholid_type() modify values. identifier type known, use normalize_scholid() convert wrapped input canonical form is_scholid() validate already-canonical values. apply checksum verification applicable. typical workflow messy data : Detect identifier types. Normalize detected type. Validate canonical identifiers. separation keeps detection permissive, normalization focused canonicalization wrapped input, validation available already-canonical strings.
code: x <- c(   "https://doi.org/10.1000/182",   "ORCID: 0000-0002-1825-0097",   "arXiv:2101.00001",   "PMID: 12345",   "not an id" ) scholid::classify_scholid(x) ## [1] NA NA NA NA NA scholid::detect_scholid_type(x) ## [1] "doi"   "orcid" "arxiv" "pmid"  NA scholid::detect_scholid_type(   c(     " 0000-0002-1825-0097 ",     " 10.1000/182 ",     "ISSN 0317-8471"   ) ) ## [1] "orcid" "doi"   "issn"

Checksum validity (control digit verify?) Registry validity (identifier actually exist?) functions scholid validate identifiers structural level verify checksums defined (ORCID, ROR, ISNI, ISBN, ISSN). check registry online existence. regexes section describe canonical form is_scholid() expects; wrapped URLs labels normalized normalize_scholid() first. text: package now supports 20 identifier types (7 0.1.1). type provides structural validation, normalization URLs labels, extraction free text via existing is_scholid(), normalize_scholid(), extract_scholid(), classify_scholid(), detect_scholid_type() APIs. New types release: ROR — Research Organization Registry iDs (checksum-validated) RRID — Research Resource Identifiers SWHID — Software Heritage persistent identifiers OpenAlex — OpenAlex entity keys (W, , S, …) bibcode — SAO/NASA ADS bibliographic codes ISNI — International Standard Name Identifier (compact form; hyphenated ORCID-shaped strings remain orcid) ARK — Archival Resource Keys (ark:/NAAN/Name) UniProt — UniProtKB accessions refseq — NCBI RefSeq accessions (versioned) sra — INSDC Sequence Read Archive accessions (SRR, SRX, SRP, …) geo — NCBI GEO accessions (GSE, GSM, GPL, GDS) bioproject — INSDC BioProject accessions (PRJNA, PRJEB, …) assembly — INSDC genome assembly accessions (GCA_, GCF_, versioned) Identifier definitions validation rules documented scholid_definitions vignette.

title: scholid 0.2.0
text: Introduced central identifier registry single source truth type names, classification order, extraction patterns, per-type metadata. Refactored per-type implementations reduce duplication; exported APIs dispatch naming convention (is_<type>, normalize_<type>, extract_<type>). Optimized classify_scholid() detect_scholid_type() avoid redundant work resolving types.
